title_en: Interpretation (I) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Law of the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 2 For a foreign-related civil relation that occurred before the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations came into force, the People's Court shall determine the applicable law in accordance with the relevant legal provisions in effect at the time of occurrence of such foreign-related civil relation; where no provision existed in the law at that time, it may determine the applicable law by reference to the provisions of the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations.

Article 3 Where the provisions of the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations are inconsistent with those of other laws on the application of law to the same foreign-related civil relation, the provisions of the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations shall apply, except for the special provisions of laws in commercial fields such as the Negotiable Instruments Law of the People's Republic of China, the Maritime Law of the People's Republic of China, the Civil Aviation Law of the People's Republic of China, and the special provisions of laws in the field of intellectual property.
Where the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations has no provisions on the application of law to a foreign-related civil relation but other laws have provisions, the provisions of such other laws shall apply.

Article 4 Where the application of law to a foreign-related civil relation involves the application of an international treaty, the People's Court shall apply such treaty in accordance with Article 142(2) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 95(1) of the Negotiable Instruments Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 268(1) of the Maritime Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 184(1) of the Civil Aviation Law of the People's Republic of China, and other legal provisions, except where the international treaty in the field of intellectual property has been or needs to be transformed into domestic law.

Article 5 Where the application of law to a foreign-related civil relation involves the application of international custom, the People's Court shall apply such custom in accordance with Article 142(3) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 95(2) of the Negotiable Instruments Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 268(2) of the Maritime Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 184(2) of the Civil Aviation Law of the People's Republic of China, and other legal provisions.

Article 6 Where the law of the People's Republic of China does not explicitly provide that the parties may choose the law applicable to a foreign-related civil relation, if the parties choose the applicable law, the People's Court shall determine that such choice is invalid.

Article 7 Where a party claims that the choice of law agreed upon by both parties is invalid on the ground that such chosen law has no actual connection with the disputed foreign-related civil relation, the People's Court shall not uphold such claim.

Article 8 Where the parties agree to choose or change the choice of the applicable law before the conclusion of the court debate in the first instance, the People's Court shall permit it.
Where each party invokes the law of the same country and does not raise any objection to the application of law, the People's Court may determine that the parties have made a choice of the law applicable to the foreign-related civil relation.

Article 9 Where the parties invoke, in a contract, an international treaty that has not yet taken effect for the People's Republic of China, the People's Court may determine the rights and obligations between the parties in accordance with the content of such international treaty, except where it violates the public interest of the People's Republic of China or the compulsory provisions of the laws and administrative regulations of the People's Republic of China.

Article 11 Where a party intentionally creates a connecting point for a foreign-related civil relation to circumvent the compulsory provisions of the laws and administrative regulations of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall determine that such action shall not have the effect of applying foreign law.

Article 12 Where the resolution of a foreign-related civil dispute depends on the determination of another foreign-related civil relation, the People's Court shall determine the applicable law for such preliminary issue according to the nature of such preliminary issue itself.
Article 13 Where a case involves two or more foreign-related civil relations, the People's Court shall separately determine the applicable laws.

Article 14 Where the parties have neither chosen the law applicable to the foreign-related arbitration agreement, nor agreed on the arbitration institution or the place of arbitration, or the agreement is unclear, the People's Court may apply the law of the People's Republic of China to determine the validity of such arbitration agreement.

Article 15 Where a natural person has continuously resided for more than one year at the time of the creation, alteration, or termination of a foreign-related civil relation and such place is the center of his or her life, the People's Court may determine it as the habitual residence of the natural person as provided in the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations, except for circumstances such as medical treatment, labor dispatch, or official business.

Article 16 The People's Court shall determine the place of establishment registration of a legal person as the place of registration of the legal person as provided in the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations.

Article 17 Where the People's Court is still unable to obtain the foreign law through reasonable means, such as provision by the parties, through channels prescribed by international treaties that have taken effect for the People's Republic of China, or provision by Chinese and foreign legal experts, it may determine that the foreign law cannot be ascertained.
Where, according to Article 10(1) of the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations, the parties shall provide the foreign law, but they fail to provide such foreign law within a reasonable time limit designated by the People's Court without justifiable reasons, the People's Court may determine that the foreign law cannot be ascertained.

Article 18 The People's Court shall hear the opinions of all parties on the content of the foreign law to be applied and its understanding and application. If the parties have no objection to the content, understanding, and application of such foreign law, the People's Court may confirm it; if the parties have objections, the People's Court shall examine and determine it.

Article 19 For the application of law to civil relations involving the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and the Macao Special Administrative Region, these Provisions shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 20 For cases involving foreign-related civil disputes that arise after the Law on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations comes into force, if the final adjudication has not been made after these Provisions come into force, these Provisions shall apply; if the final adjudication has already been made before these Provisions come into force, and the party applies for a retrial or a retrial is decided under the trial supervision procedure, these Provisions shall not apply.
Article 21 Where any previous judicial interpretation issued by this Court is inconsistent with this Interpretation, this Interpretation shall prevail.
